recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It completes the Applied clarification without changing mapping-language mechanics; any future disagreement about alias timing should be handled as a separate substantive tracker.
issue_request: FHIR-46548 was Applied/Persuasive for R6 and requested clarification that source-rule where, check, and log FHIRPath expressions are evaluated in order, that their context is the selected context.element/source element rather than the broader context identifier, that any declared alias is available, and that log records the entries that passed the earlier stages.
initial_application: Commit faa06571e3 applied the issue by adding a log bullet and a paragraph explaining that where, check, and log execute in order and that aliases are mapped before these FHIRPath statements run. That left the individual where/check/log bullets saying the expressions were evaluated on context, so the exact ambiguity identified by the issue remained in the active page.
additional_context: The mapping-language page is in current build scope through source/hierarchy.xml and is linked from the implementation-support and documentation pages. The linked Zulip thread confirms the intended alias availability and where/check/log sequencing, and FHIR-I minutes on 2024-09-09 record the Persuasive 13-0-0 vote. Focused Jira searches found no additional tightly related final issue to decide.
reconciliation: Updated source/mapping-language.html so where evaluates each candidate source element with the FHIRPath context set to that element and the alias available, check evaluates only elements that passed where, and log evaluates only elements that passed where/check. The existing sequencing paragraph was retained.
source_changes: source/mapping-language.html: Reworded the where/check/log source-rule bullets to use candidate or passed source elements as the FHIRPath context and to state alias availability and sequencing explicitly.
